idiom_name: RxJS Subject for events + BehaviorSubject or scan+shareReplay(1) for state
implementation_notes: RxJS is the library that carries the pattern in JavaScript: a Subject takes events, the reducer is an ordinary function applied with scan, and a BehaviorSubject - or a scan pipeline ending in startWith(initial) and shareReplay(1) - gives the hot state stream that replays the current state to each new subscriber; the view calls dispatch(event) and subscribes to the state stream. Where RxJS is not wanted, the same contract is expressed with a reducer store (Redux semantics: dispatch an action object, a reducer computes the next immutable state, subscribers are notified) or a small class exposing immutable state plus an EventTarget dispatcher; React binds through useSyncExternalStore and Vue through watchers. Keep states immutable and treat the event objects as the audit log.
pitfalls: Without shareReplay(1) or another multicast the pipeline is cold: each subscriber re-runs the reducer and its side effects, so two components see two different histories.
Every subscription must be unsubscribed or completed (takeUntil(destroy$)), otherwise the DOM node and its closures stay alive after the component unmounts.
Immutable updates are mandatory: mutating the state object inside scan breaks change detection and memoized selectors.
Dispatch is synchronous and unbounded: a handler that re-dispatches in a loop (search-as-you-type) queues work on the same task, so debounce or switch to a scheduled pipeline instead.
